newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended higher on Friday, fuelled by a buoyant dollar and gains in other European bonds. But record lows in long term spread yields signal that Bonos remain a fashionable asset, dealers said.
"After yesterday's move in the key money rate there is still room for further cuts which is supporting Bonos," a dealer said.
The 10-year differential over Bunds ended at 89 bps, after dipping shortly to a record low of 88 bps, with the spread to U.S. Treasuries at minus two basis points.
"The market, throughout Europe, will be driven by the strength of the U.S. dollar in the coming week," a dealer said.
The Bank of Spain shaved 25 bps off its key money rate on Thursday to 6.0 pct, but dealers added there was more to come. Some analysts expect another reduction as soon as mid February.

After yesterday's move the Spanish yield curve flattened a touch. "I expect it to remain little changed in the next week after which it should steepen further," said Robert Huw, strategist at Natwest in London.
Following a soggy mark, the peseta strengthened versus the German currency touching 83.30 but ending around 83.40/41.
